tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.

schema.name: SendFeedback
schema.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

# V15b bước 5: eval trên vault thật của user (bản B), fork v0.17.2-vantt.7

Chạy ngày 2026-11-03 trên linux-x64 (WSL2), cây `v0.17.2-vantt.7` đã dựng, bằng `quality-gate.mjs --private ... --private-detail` (gọi qua `ohs.mjs eval run` của repo dự án). Model mặc định `Xenova/multilingual-e5-small`, không rerank. Mỗi lần chạy khoảng 37 phút.

Golden set và vault nằm ngoài repo, trên máy user. Báo cáo này chỉ có số tổng hợp: không câu hỏi, không đường dẫn, không tên note.

- **Golden set:** 163 câu (153 câu holdout), 16 hạng mục, 6 đến 18 câu mỗi hạng mục.
- **Vault:** bản sao bản B, 2.082 note, **có** `_ohs/lexicon.md` (38 nhóm đồng nghĩa, 43 viết tắt, 15 từ ghép).
- **Cấu hình gói:** 1 mặc định; 2 `{"accentedFoldMinShare":0.5,"segWeightByCoverage":true}`; 3 `{"minBm25Agreement":0.2}`; 4 `{"minBm25Agreement":0}`. Cấu hình 2 đến 4 chạy bằng cách sửa tạm `pack_options` trong `vantt/scripts/quality-gates.json` vì `--private` chưa có cờ `--lang-options`.

## Tóm tắt

- Gói `vi` tăng nDCG@5 từ 0,653 lên 0,772 đến 0,776 (holdout 0,659 lên 0,771 đến 0,777). So với V15 (61 câu, không lexicon): `vi-iy`, `vi-accented`, `vi-compound` và `vi-synonym` hết tụt.
- Cấu hình 3 (`minBm25Agreement` 0,2) tốt nhất ở tổng, holdout, Hit@5 và MRR, và là cấu hình duy nhất cùng cấu hình 4 không làm `vi-typo` tụt.
- Cổng `private-regression-categories` vẫn **hỏng** ở cả bốn cấu hình: `vi-abbr` có gói kém không gói 0,081 ở mọi cấu hình. `vi-typo` tụt khoảng 0,044 ở cấu hình 1 và 2.
- Bộ cài của user giữ `v0.17.2-vantt.4` cho đến khi cổng qua.

## Tổng thể (nDCG@5, không gói 0,653, holdout 0,659)

| Cấu hình                                                | Tổng  | Holdout | Hit@1 | Hit@5 | MRR   |
| ------------------------------------------------------- | ----- | ------- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| 1 mặc định                                              | 0,772 | 0,771   | 0,736 | 0,859 | 0,784 |
| 2 `accentedFoldMinShare` 0,5 + `segWeightByCoverage`    | 0,772 | 0,771   | 0,736 | 0,859 | 0,785 |
| 3 `minBm25Agreement` 0,2                                | 0,776 | 0,777   | 0,736 | 0,871 | 0,788 |
| 4 `minBm25Agreement` 0                                  | 0,775 | 0,775   | 0,736 | 0,865 | 0,786 |

## Theo hạng mục (nDCG@5)

| Hạng mục            | Câu | Không gói | Cấu hình 1 | Cấu hình 2 | Cấu hình 3 | Cấu hình 4 |
| ------------------- | --- | --------- | ---------- | ---------- | ---------- | ---------- |
| `vi-accented`       | 8   | 0,921     | 0,918      | 0,921      | 0,923      | 0,923      |
| `vi-unaccented`     | 18  | 0,423     | 0,895      | 0,900      | 0,892      | 0,909      |
| `vi-partial-accent` | 6   | 0,820     | 0,927      | 0,900      | 0,900      | 0,900      |
| `vi-tone-placement` | 8   | 0,829     | 0,897      | 0,897      | 0,897      | 0,897      |
| `vi-iy`             | 9   | 0,878     | 0,968      | 0,968      | 0,994      | 0,994      |
| `vi-dd`             | 12  | 0,865     | 0,861      | 0,861      | 0,861      | 0,861      |
| `vi-tone-precision` | 10  | 0,776     | 0,861      | 0,861      | 0,885      | 0,885      |
| `vi-compound`       | 10  | 0,948     | 0,931      | 0,948      | 0,931      | 0,931      |
| `vi-mixed-en`       | 10  | 0,521     | 0,525      | 0,525      | 0,525      | 0,525      |
| `vi-semantic`       | 12  | 0,043     | 0,073      | 0,073      | 0,076      | 0,043      |
| `vi-names`          | 10  | 0,750     | 0,826      | 0,826      | 0,826      | 0,807      |
| `vi-telex`          | 12  | 0,428     | 0,921      | 0,910      | 0,921      | 0,921      |
| `vi-typo`           | 12  | 0,806     | 0,762      | 0,761      | 0,815      | 0,813      |
| `vi-synonym`        | 10  | 0,594     | 0,684      | 0,694      | 0,670      | 0,670      |
| `vi-abbr`           | 10  | 0,612     | 0,531      | 0,531      | 0,531      | 0,531      |
| `vi-alias`          | 6   | 0,730     | 0,979      | 0,972      | 0,972      | 0,972      |

## Cách đọc

- Hạng mục có 6 đến 18 câu: chênh khoảng 0,02 có thể là một câu đổi thứ hạng. Tổng (163 câu) đáng tin hơn.
- `vi-abbr` không đổi giữa bốn cấu hình, nên nguyên nhân không nằm ở các núm đã thử (phiếu BM25, phục hồi dấu, `seg`).
- `vi-typo` tụt ở cấu hình 1 và 2 rồi hết khi hạ `minBm25Agreement`: phiếu BM25 theo tỉ lệ đồng thuận đang đè câu gõ sai, nơi BM25 và vector hiếm khi đồng ý.
- `vi-semantic` và `vi-mixed-en` vẫn thấp ở cả hai phía: phần nghĩa (model, rerank), thuộc V22.

## Việc tiếp theo

1. Thêm cờ `--lang-options <json>` cho `quality-gate.mjs --private`, dùng chung cho lần chạy không gói và có gói.
2. Tìm nguyên nhân dạng chung cho `vi-abbr` tụt khi bật gói; cân nhắc đổi mặc định `minBm25Agreement` sang 0,2 nếu corpus sinh không tụt.
3. Đo lại reranker (V22) sau khi cổng qua.
EOF

input.description: Investigate vi-abbr pack regression
input.prompt:
Working dir: /home/vantt/projects/obsidian-hybrid-search (git repo, branch master; fork of an Obsidian hybrid search npm package). The Vietnamese language pack is `vantt/packages/ohs-lang-vi` (read its README and src/: query.ts, rescore.ts, segment-query.ts, lexicon-query.ts, core-fusion.ts, plus telex/typo/restore code). Timezone Asia/Saigon, date 2026-11-03. Reply in English.

Context: on the user's private vault (2,082 notes, with `_ohs/lexicon.md` holding 43 abbreviations, 38 synonym groups, 15 compounds), with release v0.17.2-vantt.7, category `vi-abbr` (10 queries) scores nDCG@5 0.612 without the pack and 0.531 with it, identical across these four option sets: defaults; {"accentedFoldMinShare":0.5,"segWeightByCoverage":true}; {"minBm25Agreement":0.2}; {"minBm25Agreement":0}. So the cause is not the BM25 agreement vote, accent-fold restoration share or seg weighting. Also `vi-typo` (12 q) drops 0.806 → 0.762 with defaults but is 0.815 with minBm25Agreement 0.2 (0.813 at 0); overall nDCG@5 is best at 0.2 (0.776 vs 0.772 default). Full aggregate table: `vantt/reviews/v0.17.2-vantt.7.private.md`. Plan with history of causes and fixture results: `vantt/plans/261102-1825-v15b-real-vault-regressions/plan.md`. We have NO per-query data from the vault and must never use or invent real vault content.

Tasks:
1. Find plausible generic mechanisms by which enabling the pack lowers abbreviation queries while being insensitive to those four knobs. Candidates to test with synthetic unit-level probes (write throwaway probes outside the repo or as real tests if they become regression tests): abbreviation tokens (short consonant clusters, often uppercase, e.g. like "hdsd", "kh", "dt", "tk", "ql", "cv") being reinterpreted by telex decoding (s/f/r/x/j tone keys, dd→đ, aw/ow/w), by typo correction, by unaccented→accented restoration (restoreForEmbedding sends a "restored" string to the embedder), by syllable segmentation, or by abbreviation expansion itself (abbrMaxDocShare, how the expanded phrase is weighted vs. the literal abbreviation, whether the literal token keeps its BM25 weight, case handling, lexicon parsing of `## Viết tắt` entries). Check what view terms / restored query the pack produces for such abbreviations with and without a lexicon entry.
2. For each confirmed mechanism, implement a generic fix in the pack (no query-specific hacks, no lowered thresholds), with unit tests. Add synthetic reproduction cases if needed.
3. Separately evaluate changing the default `minBm25Agreement` from 1 to 0.2 (real vault: better total and fixes vi-typo).
4. Measure with the official eval: `node vantt/eval/vi/run-eval.mjs --otf <clone of fixture repo vantt/obsidian-test-fixture at tag v0.12.0>` (see the script for args; FIXTURE_TAG is v0.12.0; there may already be a clone under /home/vantt/projects/ohs-wt/ — look, else clone there) and also on fixture v0.11.0. Acceptance: no category drops more than 0.01 nDCG@5 versus current master on either fixture (vi-synonym may drop up to 0.03), and report totals before/after. Also run the English obsidian-help check if run-eval or a sibling script supports it (it scored 0.735 with and without pack; must not drop).
5. Then write a short list of questions/shape facts the user's project-side agent should report per vi-abbr query (without revealing the query) to confirm the mechanism on the real vault — e.g. abbreviation length/case, whether it is in the lexicon, whether pack analysis shows telex/typo/restore rewriting it, rank of the right note per branch with/without pack.

Constraints:
- Work in a new git worktree under /home/vantt/projects/ohs-wt/ (e.g. `git worktree add /home/vantt/projects/ohs-wt/m-abbr -b vantt-abbr master`); never use /tmp (tmpfs quota). npm must be 12.2.0 via the wrapper /home/vantt/projects/ohs-wt/npm12.sh; set HUSKY=0 for git. A bash hook blocks commands containing the literal words "build" and "node_modules" — rephrase (npm scripts, variables) or use Read/Edit tools.
- Only change files under `vantt/**`. Keep pack tests green (`npm test` inside the pack; ~492 tests) and lint/prettier clean for changed files. Update the pack README if defaults or behaviour change.
- Commit on your branch with conventional commits (no AI references, no plan IDs in messages or code), each ending with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. Do not push or merge. Leave the worktree in place. Write a report to /home/vantt/projects/obsidian-hybrid-search/plans/reports/debugger-261103-2211-vi-abbr-regression.md with mechanisms found, fixes, eval tables (category-level), and the question list for the user side.
- If you are stuck on a design fork, you may consult the kongming agent.

End with:
Status: DONE | DONE_WITH_CONCERNS | BLOCKED | NEEDS_CONTEXT
Summary: one or two sentences
Concerns/Blockers: optional

content.text:
Em đã ghi kết quả bước 5 vào `vantt/reviews/v0.17.2-vantt.7.private.md`, chỉ số tổng hợp, không có câu hỏi hay tên note. Bước 5 trong plan V15b đã đánh dấu xong, commit và push (`0f80780`).

Tóm tắt kết quả: gói `vi` tăng nDCG@5 từ 0,653 lên 0,772–0,776. So với V15, `vi-iy`, `vi-accented`, `vi-compound` và `vi-synonym` không còn tụt. Cổng vẫn trượt vì hai hạng mục:
- **`vi-abbr`** kém không gói 0,081 ở cả bốn cấu hình. Vì không núm nào đổi được kết quả, nguyên nhân nằm ngoài phiếu BM25, phục hồi dấu và `seg`.
- **`vi-typo`** tụt khoảng 0,044 ở cấu hình 1 và 2, hết tụt khi `minBm25Agreement` bằng 0,2 hoặc 0.

Em đã bật hai agent chạy song song, chưa có kết quả:
1. **Cờ `--lang-options <json>` cho `quality-gate --private`:** áp dụng chung cho lần chạy không gói và có gói, và ghi tuỳ chọn đã dùng vào báo cáo để phân biệt các lần chạy. Bên dự án sẽ không phải sửa tạm `quality-gates.json` nữa.
2. **Nguyên nhân dạng chung của `vi-abbr`:** agent kiểm xem viết tắt có bị telex, sửa lỗi gõ, phục hồi dấu, tách âm tiết hoặc bước mở rộng viết tắt hiểu sai không. Agent cũng thử đổi mặc định `minBm25Agreement` sang 0,2. Mỗi sửa phải qua eval trên fixture v0.12.0 và v0.11.0, không hạng mục nào được tụt quá 0,01.

**Nhờ bên dự án gửi phân tích `vi-abbr` theo dạng câu** (không kèm câu thật). Với từng câu trong 10 câu, cần các thông tin sau:
- Độ dài viết tắt, viết hoa hay thường, và có trong `## Viết tắt` của lexicon không.
- Câu chỉ có viết tắt hay có thêm từ khác.
- Phần phân tích của gói (`--private-detail`) có viết lại viết tắt không: telex, sửa lỗi gõ, phục hồi dấu hay tách âm tiết.
- Hạng của note đúng ở từng nhánh (fulltext, semantic, hybrid), khi có gói và khi không gói.
- Cụm đầy đủ của viết tắt có nằm trong note đúng không, và có phổ biến trong vault không (khoảng bao nhiêu phần trăm số note).

Bản cài `C:\tools\ohs` giữ vantt.4 cho đến khi cổng qua. Hai agent xong thì em gộp vào master, đo lại và báo anh.

**How it behaves**
- **Parsing:** the value must be a JSON object. If it isn't, the report gets a fixed error, the gate exits 2 and nothing runs. The two errors are `--lang-options is not valid JSON` and `--lang-options must be a JSON object`. Neither repeats the input, because the options can hold a vault path in `lexiconPath`. - **Override:** it replaces `config.pack_options[lang]` for the run. Without the flag, the options in `quality-gates.json` are used as before.
- **Both runs get the same options:** I changed `packEnv` to take the options themselves instead of looking them up in the config. The private runs now use one value: the with-pack run receives it as `OHS_LANGUAGE_PACK_OPTIONS`. The no-pack run gets no pack options (the eval environment drops all `OHS_*` variables). Both runs pass the same options to `privateEvalEnv`, so they skip the same lexicon file and index the same notes. The `--private-detail` runs follow the same rule. I updated the comment in `eval-run.mjs` that documents this rule.
- **Report:** there was no existing field, so I added `pack_options` to the private report. It holds the effective options, or `null` when there are none. The `--private-detail` file records it too.
- **Non-private mode:** the flag is rejected outside `--private` with exit 2 and `--lang-options is only valid with --private (the release gate uses pack_options in quality-gates.json)`. That mode is the release gate, which writes baselines against the reviewed config. It also accepts several `--with-lang` values, so it would be unclear which pack the options belong to.

**Tests** (`vantt/scripts/test/quality-gate.test.mjs`)
- Unit tests for `parseLangOptions`: valid objects, invalid JSON, and non-objects (`null`, an array, a string, a number, a boolean).
- The stub eval and search now record the pack settings each run receives. CLI tests use them to check four things:
  - The flag overrides the configured options and both runs get the same lexicon ignore.
  - The detail runs and the detail file get the options too.
  - The report records the configured options, or `null`, when the flag is absent.
  - The flag is rejected outside `--private`.
- To inject a test config, `main()` now accepts an optional `config` argument. Without it, `main()` reads `quality-gates.json` as before.

**Docs:** I updated the usage comment in `quality-gate.mjs` and the private-vault section of `vantt/eval/vi/README.md`, which is where `--private` is documented in detail. `vantt/README.md` only mentions `--private` in a list, so I left it unchanged.

The report records the options as given, so a `lexiconPath` value appears in it. That path is configuration rather than note content, but the README now says not to put note names or real content in the options.

Status: DONE_WITH_CONCERNS
Summary: `--lang-options` works in `--private` mode, gives the same options to both runs, records them as `pack_options`, and is rejected outside `--private`. The work is on `vantt-langopt` as commit `910b770`, with lint and all vantt script tests passing.
Concerns/Blockers: I installed dependencies with `npm ci --ignore-scripts`, which skips package build steps. That doesn't matter for these stub-based tests, but a real private run from this worktree may need a normal install first.</result>

<result>I found the cause of the `vi-abbr` drop, reproduced it on a small made-up vault run through the real core, and fixed it. The fix is not yet confirmed on your real vault; the next real-vault run will show that. All four tasks are done, and the branch passes the acceptance check on both fixtures.

**The main cause.** A query with diacritics that contains an abbreviation, like `quy trình chăm sóc KH`, normally doesn't use the pack's `norm` and `fold` views. When the lexicon matched, the pack filled those two views with the expansion alone (`khách hàng` / `khach hang`). That created two extra ranking branches (weights 1.5 and 0.75) that voted for whichever notes contain `khách hàng` most often, ignoring the rest of the query.

None of your four option sets could affect this:
- `KH` is not a Vietnamese syllable, so the BM25 agreement penalty is skipped for the query.
- For the same reason, the `seg` branch doesn't run.
- `accentedFoldMinShare` only looks at pairs of syllables.

On the made-up vault (34 notes, 7 queries with diacritics and an abbreviation):

| Setup | nDCG@5 |
| --- | --- |
| No pack | 1.000 |
| Master pack | 0.698 (one query 1→0, one 1→0.5, one 1→0.387) |
| Master pack, lexicon disabled | 1.000 |
| Master pack, your alternative options | 0.698 |
| Fixed pack | 1.000 |

The fixtures can't show this problem: their `vi-abbr` target notes have the expanded phrase as the title, so they already score 1.000 with the old code.

**Commits on `vantt-abbr`** (not pushed or merged):
1. `34080b3`: an abbreviation's expansion now goes into the upstream BM25 query, where it is ranked together with the rest of the query. It is added only to views the query already searches. Its BM25 query is visible in `debug.baseQuery`.
   - Synonyms keep the old behaviour. Applying the new rule to them cost `vi-synonym` 0.16 on both fixtures.
2. `f735f0e`: a word of two or more capital letters is treated as an acronym. It is no longer given diacritics, decoded as Telex or typo-corrected. Before, `BA` became `ba`/`bà` at 50% each. The exception is a multi-word query typed entirely in capitals.
3. `07e6bc5`: a query with a corrected typo keeps its BM25 votes. The vector branch embedded the misspelled text, so its disagreement with BM25 isn't evidence against BM25. On your vault, turning the check off gave `vi-typo` 0.813, against 0.762 with the default.
4. `327c555`: updated the pack README and the V15b plan; the plan also has the question list in Vietnamese.

Pack tests pass (495, up from 492), and type checking, lint and Prettier are clean. I did not run the repo-level `npm run verify:task`; only pack files changed.

**Nguyên nhân:** câu có dấu mà chứa viết tắt, như `quy trình chăm sóc KH`. Khi khớp lexicon, gói tạo thêm hai nhánh xếp hạng chỉ từ cụm đầy đủ (`khách hàng`). Hai nhánh này kéo lên những note nhắc `khách hàng` nhiều nhất, bất kể phần còn lại của câu. Cả bốn núm anh thử đều không chạm tới đường này, nên `vi-abbr` y hệt nhau ở mọi cấu hình.

Nhánh có ba sửa:
- **Viết tắt:** cụm đầy đủ được tìm cùng phần còn lại của câu, không còn đứng riêng thành nhánh.
- **Từ viết hoa từ 2 chữ trở lên** (`BA`, `KH`) được coi là viết tắt: không thêm dấu, không đọc theo telex, không sửa lỗi gõ. Trước đây `BA` bị đoán thành `ba` hoặc `bà`.
- **Câu gõ sai đã được sửa:** không còn bị trừ phiếu BM25. Đây là nguyên nhân `vi-typo` tụt ở cấu hình mặc định.

**Kết quả đo:**

| Bộ đo | Trước sửa | Sau sửa |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Vault giả lập tái hiện lỗi (7 câu) | 0,698 | 1,000 (bằng không gói) |
| Fixture v0.12.0 | 0,914 | 0,914 |
| Fixture v0.11.0 | 0,961 | 0,961 |

Trên hai fixture, mọi hạng mục giữ nguyên. Bộ tiếng Anh vẫn 0,735. Hai fixture không thấy được lỗi này, vì note đích của `vi-abbr` ở đó có sẵn cụm đầy đủ trong tiêu đề.

**`minBm25Agreement`:** em giữ mặc định 1, không đổi sang 0,2. Trên fixture, 0,2 làm `vi-semantic` tụt 0,024–0,034, vượt ngưỡng 0,01. Cái lợi cho `vi-typo` mà 0,2 mang lại thì sửa thứ ba đã lấy được, mà không tụt chỗ khác.

**Hai chỗ em chưa sửa:**
- Viết tắt viết thường trùng với một từ thường vẫn bị mở rộng. Ví dụ, nếu lexicon có `da = dự án`, câu `kem dưỡng da mặt` sẽ bị thêm `dự án`.
- Đồng nghĩa trong câu dài có dấu có cùng dạng lỗi, nhưng sửa thì fixture tụt 0,16. `vi-synonym` trên vault của anh vốn đã tăng khi bật gói, nên em để nguyên.

<result>## Code Review Summary: vantt-abbr, `vantt/packages/ohs-lang-vi`

### Scope
- Files: `src/lexicon-query.ts`, `src/query.ts`, `src/rescore.ts`, `src/rewrite.ts`, two test files, README. About 190 lines changed.
- How I checked: the pack tests pass on the branch (15 files, 495 tests). I ran the same probe queries through `analyzeQuery` on master and on the branch, using `fakeContext` and a real lexicon file. I also ran FTS5 with the upstream tokenizer (`unicode61 tokenchars '+#'`) to see how BM25 scores the new base queries. The probe files were written under `/home/vantt/projects/ohs-wt/tmp/probe` and deleted afterwards. No repo files changed.

### High

**1. Accented words typed in capitals are treated as acronyms. This turns the pack off or drops branches for ordinary Vietnamese.** `src/query.ts:103` (`CAPITALS_RE`), used by `acronymIndexes` (`query.ts:110-117`).
`\p{Lu}` matches any capital letter, so `ĐẠI`, `HỌC`, `HÀNG` and `NGÀY` all count as acronyms. Their `syllable` flag becomes false, which then affects `isVietnameseQuery`, `literalToken` and the seg view's check that every token is a syllable (`segment-query.ts:65`). Master compared with the branch:
- `trường ĐẠI HỌC`: vietnamese true becomes false, and the pack stops acting on it.
- `Khách HÀNG tiềm năng`: seg view `khách_hàng tiềm_năng` becomes null. `literalToken` becomes true, so the weak-BM25 check is skipped.
- `NGÀY` (one-word query): vietnamese true becomes false.

Real acronyms almost never carry vowel or tone marks; the README's examples are `BA`, `DA`, `KH`, and `HĐ`/`ĐKKD` only use Đ.
- **Fix:** limit acronym letters to A–Z plus Đ and digits, for example `/^(?=(?:[^A-ZĐ]*[A-ZĐ]){2})[A-ZĐ0-9]+$/u`. Another option is to require `foldToken(norm) === norm` after mapping đ to d.
- **Tests to add:** `trường ĐẠI HỌC` stays Vietnamese, and `Khách HÀNG tiềm năng` keeps its seg view.

### Medium

**2. The expanded BM25 base query counts some words twice.** `src/lexicon-query.ts:44-45` together with `extend` (`:17-22`).
`extend` only removes exact duplicates. The upstream tokenizer strips some diacritics (with its default setting, `năng`, `khách`, `hàng` and `trình` lose their marks, but `tiềm` keeps its mark). Because the upstream BM25 query ORs every term, a repeated term adds its score twice.
- Branch output for `khach hang KH`: base is `khach hang kh khách hàng tiềm năng`. `khach`/`khách` and `hang`/`hàng` each appear twice, and the prefix term `kh` matches `khach` a third time.
- Branch output for `kh tiem nang` (lexicon `KH = khách hàng = khách hàng tiềm năng`): base is `kh tiem nang khách hàng tiềm năng`, so `nang`/`năng` appears twice.
- In the FTS5 run, a note containing only `tiem nang khach hang` moved from -2.348 to -3.169 just from adding `"năng"*`.

So the expansion over-weights words the user already typed, which is a smaller version of the problem this change is meant to fix.
- **Fix:** in `addExpansions`, when extending `baseQuery`, skip an expansion word whose `foldWord(w)` matches the fold of any word already in the base. Keep exact-match removal for the views.

**3. Abbreviations that are also Vietnamese syllables still expand when typed in lowercase or caps lock, and the expansion now also goes into upstream BM25.** `src/lexicon.ts:194-206` (unaccented words match by folded form) together with `lexicon-query.ts:43-45`.
- `ba ngay` gives base `ba ngay business analyst`. On master, `ba ngay` had no base query; the expansion was only in norm/fold.
- `BA NGAY` (caps lock) behaves the same.
- `ai la gi` gives base `ai la gi trí tuệ nhân tạo`.

This contradicts the new rule that lowercase `ba` is a syllable; the new test asserts exactly that at `lexicon.test.ts`, "takes a word typed in capitals…". For `ai la gi` the branch is actually better than master, which ran the expansion alone in the norm view. For `ba ngay` it adds a wrong expansion to a branch that weighs 1.5 in fulltext mode.
- **Fix:** if an abbreviation's form is itself a possible Vietnamese syllable (`ba`, `da`, `ai`), expand it only when the query token has `acronym === true`. Abbreviations that cannot be syllables, such as `kh`, `hđ` and `c++`, keep matching case-insensitively.
- **Test to add:** assert `baseQuery` for `ba ngay`.

### Low

**4. The typo exemption fires whenever any word is "corrected", including correct words the vault just doesn't contain.** `src/query.ts:300` together with `rescore.ts:162-163`.
- Example: `hd mua ban` in a vault without `ban` gives `rewrite.typo=[2]` (`ban` becomes `an`), so `typoCorrected` is true and the BM25 check is skipped for the whole query.
- Also, when only typo correction fired (no Telex), `baseQuery` is not set to the corrected text. Upstream BM25 still searches the misspelled words (`giu chna khahc hang …`), so the BM25 votes this exemption keeps come from a query that never got the correction.
- This matches the measured trade-off in the README, so it is a risk note rather than a bug. Consider limiting the exemption to cases where the corrected word is a real token of the query, or making it proportional.

**5. `debug.baseQuery` is only recorded on the lexicon path** (`lexicon-query.ts:109-112`). When only Telex sets `baseQuery` (`query.ts:306`), explain shows it only as `rewrite.text`. Minor inconsistency.

**6. A side effect of change 2 that isn't tested.** Any query with a capitals word (`hop dong IT`, `tuyen BA`, `AI là gì`) now has `literalToken=true`, which turns off the seg branch and the weak-BM25 check. `hop dong IT` lost seg `hợp_đồng` compared with master. The README's "không tính là âm tiết" ("not counted as a syllable") documents this, but no test pins it down.

### Checked, no finding
- **FTS5 syntax safety:** the base query only contains words from `state.normalized` and lexicon words limited to letters, numbers, marks, `+` and `#`. Upstream `sanitizeFtsQuery` and `toFtsQuery` then strip `" * ^ ( )` and quote each word. `"KH" OR tiềm` becomes `"kh" or tiềm …` and `KH: tiềm*` becomes `kh: tiềm* …`, both harmless. `C++` stays a single token, which the `+#` tokenchars setting supports.
- **Empty expansions:** removed at parse time (`form.length > 0`). If the commonness check drops every expansion, `abbreviationWords` is empty and `baseQuery` is untouched.
- **Multiple expansions and repeated abbreviations** (`KH HĐ`, `KH KH`): no duplicate terms beyond the folding issue in finding 2.
- **No lexicon, or synonyms only:** `applyLexicon` returns early, or `baseQuery` is left alone. The synonym path is unchanged.
- **Acronym edge cases:** single letters (`A B`), mixed case (`KHách`) and `Đ` alone are not acronyms. `B2B`, `IT`, `SE3` and `ĐKKD` are. If the raw and normalized token counts differ, the code falls back to no acronyms. Telex rewriting never replaces an acronym token, because acronyms count as known words.
- **Multi-query rank-key prefix:** this diff doesn't touch it. A problem that already existed on master: after a multi-query fan-out, ranks are keyed `0:bm25` and so on, but `rescore` reads `rank.bm25`, `rank.semantic` and `rank['view:norm']`. So the weak-BM25 check (including the new typo exemption), the norm-rank bonus and the semantic term never take effect in multi-query searches.

### Test coverage gaps
- No case with accented capitals (finding 1).
- No check for words repeated after folding in `baseQuery` (finding 2).

An independent review of vantt-abbr found these issues. Please fix them on the same branch and worktree (/home/vantt/projects/ohs-wt/m-abbr), under the same constraints as before. Reply in English.

1. HIGH, src/query.ts:103 CAPITALS_RE: `\p{Lu}` makes accented all-caps words such as ĐẠI, HỌC, HÀNG and NGÀY count as acronyms. That breaks `trường ĐẠI HỌC`, where the query is no longer treated as Vietnamese, `Khách HÀNG tiềm năng`, where the seg view becomes null and literalToken turns true, and a one-word `NGÀY`. Limit acronym letters to A–Z, Đ and digits, for example `/^(?=(?:[^A-ZĐ]*[A-ZĐ]){2})[A-ZĐ0-9]+$/u`, and add regression tests.
2. MEDIUM, lexicon-query.ts:17-22 and 44-45: the expanded baseQuery repeats words once folded, because the upstream tokenizer strips some diacritics. `khach hang KH` becomes `khach hang kh khách hàng tiềm năng`, and `kh tiem nang` gives `nang`/`năng` twice. FTS5 adds the score of each repeated term. When you extend baseQuery, skip an expansion word whose fold matches a word already there. Add a test.
3. MEDIUM, lexicon.ts:194-206 and lexicon-query.ts:43-45: an abbreviation whose form is itself a possible Vietnamese syllable (ba, da, ai) still expands when typed in lowercase or with caps lock, and the expansion now also goes into BM25. `ba ngay` becomes `ba ngay business analyst`. Expand a syllable-shaped abbreviation only when the query token is an acronym. Non-syllable forms (kh, hđ, c++) keep matching case-insensitively. Add a `ba ngay` baseQuery test. Watch `ai la gi`: the reviewer said the branch beats master there, so check the fixtures' vi-abbr queries before deciding.
4. LOW: the typo exemption fires whenever any word gets "corrected", even a correct word the vault lacks (`hd mua ban` turns `ban` into `an`). Also, when only typo correction fires, baseQuery is not the corrected text, so upstream BM25 still searches the misspelled words. Try narrowing the exemption, and/or set baseQuery to the corrected text. Keep a change only if both fixtures pass the acceptance rule.
5. LOW: record debug.baseQuery on the Telex-only path too, not only on the lexicon path.
6. Add a test that pins the documented side effect: a capitals word (`hop dong IT`) sets literalToken, which turns off seg.
7. Optional, as a separate commit only if it is eval-neutral or better: rescore reads rank.bm25, rank.semantic and rank['view:norm'], but after a multi-query fan-out the keys carry a prefix (`0:bm25`). The weak-BM25 check, the typo exemption, the norm bonus and the semantic term therefore never fire in multi-query searches. Check the P01 contract in vantt/patches/0001-language-pack-api.patch for the key format before changing anything.

Then re-run the official eval on v0.12.0 and v0.11.0 (category-level, same acceptance rule), the English check, and your synthetic abbreviation vault. Run the pack tests, tsc, lint and prettier. Review độc lập tìm ra một lỗi nặng và hai lỗi vừa trên nhánh `vantt-abbr`. Em chưa gộp gì vào master, vì sửa xong cả ba thì mới an toàn cho tiếng Việt thường. Em đã gửi các lỗi lại cho agent đã viết nhánh này để sửa.

- **Lỗi nặng:** chữ in hoa có dấu như `ĐẠI HỌC` hay `NGÀY` bị coi là viết tắt. Câu `trường ĐẠI HỌC` khi đó không còn được xử lý như tiếng Việt. Cách sửa là chỉ coi là viết tắt khi chữ gồm A–Z, Đ và số.
- **Lỗi vừa 1:** khi chèn cụm đầy đủ của viết tắt vào câu tìm, một số từ bị lặp sau khi bỏ dấu (`khach` và `khách`), nên được tính điểm hai lần.
- **Lỗi vừa 2:** viết tắt trùng với một âm tiết tiếng Việt (`ba`, `ai`) vẫn bị mở rộng khi gõ chữ thường. Ví dụ `ba ngay` bị thêm `business analyst`. Cách sửa là chỉ mở rộng khi người dùng gõ in hoa (`BA`).

Agent cũng xem hai điểm nhỏ về câu gõ sai. Ngoài ra, agent sẽ thử sửa một lỗi có từ trước: khi một câu được tách thành nhiều câu con để tìm, các bước chấm lại điểm của gói không chạy. Phần này chỉ giữ nếu fixture không tụt.

Sau đó agent chạy lại eval trên cả hai fixture và bộ tiếng Anh. Có kết quả em sẽ gộp vào master để CI ra bản `vantt.8`, rồi báo anh.

content.text:
Bản `v0.17.2-vantt.8` đã phát hành và là bản Latest, có gói Windows, Linux và Mac chip M kèm sha256. Mac Intel vẫn bị chặn như anh đã chốt; ghi chú phát hành dẫn máy Intel sang vantt.4. Không còn issue nào mở. README và plan đã cập nhật và push. Em đã xoá các worktree, nhánh và file tạm đã xong việc, chỉ giữ hai bản clone fixture để đo lại.

So với vantt.7, bản này có:
- **`quality-gate --private` có cờ `--lang-options '<json>'`.** Bên dự án không cần sửa tạm `quality-gates.json` nữa.
- **Sửa nguyên nhân `vi-abbr` tụt:** cụm đầy đủ của viết tắt giờ được tìm cùng phần còn lại của câu.
- **Từ in hoa gồm A–Z, Đ, số (`KH`, `BA`) được coi là viết tắt.** Chữ in hoa có dấu như `ĐẠI HỌC` vẫn là tiếng Việt thường.
- **Câu gõ sai đã được sửa giữ phiếu BM25:** đây là cách sửa trực tiếp chỗ `vi-typo` tụt. `minBm25Agreement` giữ mặc định 1.
- **Trên hai fixture (v0.12.0 và v0.11.0):** mọi hạng mục bằng bản trước. Bộ tiếng Anh cũng giữ nguyên.

Việc tiếp theo cần bên dự án: chạy lại V15 trên vault thật bằng vantt.8. Một lần mặc định là đủ. Nếu cổng qua thì nâng `C:\tools\ohs` lên vantt.8. Nếu `vi-abbr` vẫn tụt, nhờ gửi phân tích theo dạng câu như em đã liệt kê; danh sách đầy đủ có trong plan V15b.

Một điểm cần biết khi chạy: viết tắt trùng với một âm tiết (`ba`, `da`, `ai`) giờ chỉ được mở rộng khi gõ in hoa.

content: Mục tiêu là gói `vi` không lỗi và tìm tốt nhất trên vault thật. Bản sửa `vi-abbr` và `vi-typo` đã ra trong `v0.17.2-vantt.8` (Latest). Việc tiếp theo: bên dự án chạy lại V15 trên vault thật bằng vantt.8.

content.text:
Kế hoạch của anh ổn, nhưng nó khớp với repo **momentry**, không phải repo này. `windows-hook-probe.yml` và nhánh `main` chỉ có ở `vantt/momentry`. Repo `obsidian-hybrid-search` dùng nhánh `master` và không có file đó. Em chưa sửa gì ở cả hai repo.

**Giới hạn đang gặp có lẽ là số job chạy cùng lúc.** Cả hai repo đều public, nên runner chuẩn không bị tính phút. Gói Free giới hạn khoảng 20 job chạy song song, trong đó chỉ 5 job macOS. Trong khoảng 30 lần chạy gần nhất của momentry, `ci` chạy 18 lần khi push. Mỗi lần là 9 job, trong đó 3 job macOS, nên hàng đợi macOS nghẽn trước.

**Kế hoạch cho momentry, em đề xuất bổ sung bốn điểm:**
1. **Push vào `main` và PR:** chạy Linux với Node 20, 22, 24, cộng một job Windows với Node 22. Tổng 4 job thay vì 9, và không còn job macOS nào.
2. **Ma trận đầy đủ:** `release.yml` đang gọi `ci.yml` qua `workflow_call`. Em sẽ thêm một input `full: true` cho lời gọi đó, và thêm `workflow_dispatch` để anh chạy tay được.
3. **`concurrency` với `cancel-in-progress`:** push liên tiếp sẽ huỷ lần chạy cũ, đỡ tốn hàng đợi.
4. **`windows-hook-probe.yml`:** hiện đã chỉ chạy tay, nhưng có 10 lần chạy tay gần đây. Thêm trigger theo đường dẫn phần hook Windows thì cần biết thư mục nào là phần hook. Em sẽ tự tìm trong repo.

**Repo này cũng có chỗ nặng tương tự, ở workflow khác.** Mỗi lần push vào `vantt/packages/**` hay `vantt/patches/**` đều kéo theo `vantt-bundles`. Workflow này chạy 2 job dựng gói macOS, 2 job smoke macOS và khoảng 4 job kiểm pin-effect và eval cho Mac Intel. Mac Intel lại luôn bị chặn, theo quyết định anh đã chốt. Em đề xuất:
- Bỏ hẳn dựng và đo darwin-x64 trong luồng tự động, chỉ chạy khi gọi tay với `only=darwin-x64`.
- Thêm `concurrency` cho `vantt-catchup`.

Hai thay đổi này bớt được khoảng 4–6 job macOS mỗi lần phát hành. Mac Intel vẫn không có gói, giống hiện nay.

Anh muốn em làm phần nào: momentry theo kế hoạch trên, repo này, hay cả hai?

content: Mục tiêu là thu gọn ma trận CI cho hợp giới hạn của GitHub; kế hoạch anh đưa khớp repo momentry, còn repo này nặng ở bước dựng gói macOS. Anh chọn giúp em làm momentry, repo này, hay cả hai.

env:
  HUSKY: '0'

  GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
  TAG: ${{ inputs.tag || github.ref_name }}

jobs:
  prepare:
    if: github.repository == 'vantt/obsidian-hybrid-search'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - name: Validate tag and make sure the release exists
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if ! [[ "$TAG" =~ ^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+-vantt\.[0-9]+$ ]]; then
            echo "::error::$TAG is not a fork release tag (v<semver>-vantt.<N>)"
            exit 1
          fi
          git ls-remote --exit-code --tags "https://github.com/$GH_REPO" "refs/tags/$TAG" >/dev/null \
            || { echo "::error::tag $TAG does not exist on $GH_REPO"; exit 1; }
          # Not marked latest until every platform has passed (done in the release job).
          if ! gh release view "$TAG" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            gh release create "$TAG" --verify-tag --latest=false --title "OHS ${TAG#v}" \
              --notes "Bundles for $TAG are being built: $GITHUB_SERVER_URL/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs/$GITHUB_RUN_ID"
          fi

  bundle:
    needs: prepare
    if: ${{ inputs.reuse_run == '' && inputs.only == '' }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - platform: win32-x64
            runner: windows-latest
          - platform: darwin-arm64
            runner: macos-14
          # onnxruntime-node 1.30 ships no darwin/x64 binding; bundle.mjs substitutes the newest version
          # that has one (PLATFORM_PINS) for this platform only, and the parity job checks the result.
          - platform: darwin-x64
            runner: macos-15-intel
          - platform: linux-x64
            runner: ubuntu-latest
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    timeout-minutes: 45
    defaults:

        with:

      - uses: actions/setup-node@49933ea5288caeca8642d1e84afbd3f7d6820020 # v4.4.0
        with:
          node-version-file: tree/.node-version
          cache: ''

      # Upstream refuses other npm versions (devEngines.packageManager).
      - name: Pin npm 12.2.0

name: vantt-bundles

# build on each platform's native runner, smoke test the bundle on a runner that
# only has the archive (no setup-node), then attach bundles and checksums to the
# GitHub Release for the tag. Not signed on macOS (PRD 8.3, Q4).
#
# There is no push-tag trigger on purpose: a tag start would run the workflow file
# of the tagged commit, but release branches carry no .github/workflows (upstream's
# are removed), and tags pushed with GITHUB_TOKEN start nothing anyway. Run it from
# master: dispatch with the tag, or call it from catchup (workflow_call).

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tag:
        description: 'Fork release tag, e.g. v0.17.2-vantt.1'
        required: true
      only:
        description: 'Set to pin-effect to run only that check (measurement, no build, smoke or publishing)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      reuse_run:
        description: 'Run id of an earlier vantt-bundles run: skip the build and re-test/re-release its bundle artifacts'
        required: false
        default: ''
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      tag:
        description: 'Fork release tag'
        required: true
        type: string

permissions:
  contents: write

  smoke:
    needs: [prepare, bundle, pin-effect]
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && inputs.only == '' && needs.prepare.result == 'success' && (needs.bundle.result == 'success' || needs.bundle.result == 'skipped') }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - platform: win32-x64
            runner: windows-latest
          - platform: darwin-arm64
            runner: macos-14
          - platform: darwin-x64
            runner: macos-15-intel
          - platform: linux-x64
            runner: ubuntu-latest

    timeout-minutes: 45

      run:
        shell: bash

      # No setup-node and no npm: the bundle must run on its own Node. The runner's
      # own Node only drives the test script.
      - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683 # v4.2.2

          ref: master
          path: tools
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@d3f86a106a0bac45b974a628896c90dbdf5c8093 # v4.3.0
        with:
          name: bundle-${{ matrix.platform }}
          if-no-files-found: ignore

      # darwin-x64 also needs the pin-effect check (job pin-effect) to have passed.
      - name: Upload this platform's bundle to the release
        if: ${{ success() && (matrix.platform != 'darwin-x64' || needs.pin-effect.outputs.ok == 'true') }}
        run: gh release upload "$TAG" "$RUNNER_TEMP"/in/ohs-* --clobber

      - name: Fail visibly when the pin-effect check did not pass
        if: ${{ success() && matrix.platform == 'darwin-x64' && needs.pin-effect.outputs.ok != 'true' }}
        run: |
          echo "::error::darwin-x64 was not published: onnxruntime-node 1.23.2 changes nDCG@5 by more than 0.01 against 1.30.0 on the same machine (see job pin-effect)"

  # 1.30.0 against the 1.23.2 that the darwin-x64 bundle ships (PRD 8.4, step 6). The numbers of quantised ONNX
  # models depend on the runner's CPU, so the check only counts on the CPU class it was calibrated
  # on (AMD EPYC); another class retries on a fresh runner, up to three attempts.

    needs: prepare
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.prepare.result == 'success' }}
    uses: ./.github/workflows/vantt-pin-effect.yml
    with:
      tag: ${{ inputs.tag || github.ref_name }}
      attempt: 1
  pe2:
    needs: [prepare, pe1]
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.prepare.result == 'success' && needs.pe1.outputs.inconclusive == 'true' }}
    uses: ./.github/workflows/vantt-pin-effect.yml

  # Without one (three other CPUs in a row) the verdict is "not ok" and says so.
  pin-effect:
    needs: [pe1, pe2, pe3]
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.pe1.result != 'skipped' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    outputs:
      ok: ${{ steps.verdict.outputs.ok }}
    steps:
      - id: verdict
        env:
          O1: ${{ needs.pe1.outputs.inconclusive }}
          K1: ${{ needs.pe1.outputs.ok }}
          O2: ${{ needs.pe2.outputs.inconclusive }}
          K2: ${{ needs.pe2.outputs.ok }}
          O3: ${{ needs.pe3.outputs.inconclusive }}
          K3: ${{ needs.pe3.outputs.ok }}

          ok=false
          if [ "$O1" = false ]; then ok=$K1
          elif [ "$O2" = false ]; then ok=$K2
          elif [ "$O3" = false ]; then ok=$K3

    runs-on: macos-15-intel
    continue-on-error: true
    timeout-minutes: 90
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash

      - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683 # v4.2.2
        with:
          ref: refs/tags/${{ env.TAG }}

          persist-credentials: false

          path: tools
          persist-credentials: false

        run: npm install -g npm@12.2.0 && npm --version
      - uses: actions/cache@0057852bfaa89a56745cba8c7296529d2fc39830 # v4.3.0
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/huggingface

      - name: Install the release tree and build the Vietnamese pack
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          (cd tree && npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund)
          # onnxruntime-node's install script downloads binaries and fails on network hiccups
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do (cd tree && npm rebuild) && break; [ "$attempt" = 3 ] && exit 1; sleep 15; done
          cp -R tree/vantt/packages/ohs-lang-vi "$RUNNER_TEMP/ohs-lang-vi"

          fixture_tag=$(grep -m1 '^const FIXTURE_TAG' tools/vantt/eval/vi/run-eval.mjs | cut -d"'" -f2)

        run: |
          node tools/vantt/scripts/bundle-parity.mjs run --tree tree --out "$RUNNER_TEMP/eval" \

        with:
          name: eval-darwin-x64
          path: |
            ${{ runner.temp }}/eval/obsidian-help.json
            ${{ runner.temp }}/eval/vi.json
          if-no-files-found: error

    needs: [prepare, smoke, pin-effect]
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && inputs.only == '' && needs.prepare.result == 'success' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:

        with:
          ref: master
          path: tools
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@d3f86a106a0bac45b974a628896c90dbdf5c8093 # v4.3.0
        with:
          path: artifacts
      - name: Write notes
        env:

content.text:
Em đã thu gọn CI cho repo này và push lên master (`327c995`). Repo này không cần làm như kế hoạch của anh cho momentry. CI gốc của upstream (`ci.yml`, ma trận 3 hệ điều hành × 3 bản Node) vốn đã tắt trên fork. Trên fork chỉ có các workflow `vantt-*` chạy. Trong đó `vantt-pr-check` chỉ có một job Ubuntu, nên không cần đụng.

Chỗ chiếm runner macOS là mỗi lần phát hành. Mỗi lần push vào `vantt/packages/**` hoặc `vantt/patches/**`, catchup ra một bản mới và `vantt-bundles` chạy cho bản đó. Trong số job của `vantt-bundles` có 5 job macOS, trong đó 3 job là cho Mac Intel, cùng tối đa 3 lần kiểm pin-effect. Mà gói Intel lần nào cũng bị chặn, như anh đã chốt.

Thay đổi:
- **Mặc định không dựng, kiểm hay đo gói Mac Intel nữa.** Mỗi lần phát hành còn 2 job macOS (Mac chip M) thay vì 5, và không còn lần kiểm pin-effect nào.
- **Muốn có gói Intel thì chạy tay** `vantt-bundles` với ô `darwin_x64` bật. Khi đó mọi thứ chạy như cũ, kể cả bước chặn.
- **Ghi chú phát hành tự thêm dòng "Mac Intel"** dẫn tới README, và bản mới vẫn tự được đánh dấu Latest khi cả 3 nền qua. Trước đây em phải làm hai việc này bằng tay.
- README của fork đã ghi ô `darwin_x64`.

Em đang chạy lại bản vantt.8 từ các gói đã dựng sẵn để kiểm cấu hình mới trên GitHub thật. Lần này chỉ smoke 3 nền và ghi lại release notes, không dựng lại. Có kết quả em báo anh.

Còn momentry, kế hoạch của anh hợp lý, kèm 4 điểm bổ sung em đã nêu ở tin trước. Anh muốn thì em làm luôn.

content.text:
Em đã gộp nhánh `bundle-license-notices` vào master và push (`6a184b7`), rồi xoá nhánh cả trên máy lẫn trên GitHub. Master không có commit nào mới hơn nhánh, nên chỉ cần tiến master lên, không có xung đột.

Trước khi gộp em đã chạy test trên nhánh, và tất cả đều qua:
- 158 test script của fork, tăng 8 test nhờ phần giấy phép.
- 499 test của gói `vi`.
- Lint và prettier sạch.

Nhánh có hai thay đổi:
- **Gói `ohs-lang-vi` theo giấy phép độc quyền riêng:** chỉ được dùng cùng `pkm` theo EULA. Phần còn lại của fork vẫn MIT, giống upstream.
- **Mỗi gói npm đi kèm bundle đều có file giấy phép.** Gói nào không tự kèm file thì `bundle.mjs` lấy bản chuẩn trong `vantt/licenses/`. Nếu gặp một giấy phép chưa có bản chuẩn, việc dựng bundle sẽ dừng với lỗi chứ không bỏ qua gói đó.

Push này đã khởi chạy catchup và sẽ ra bản `v0.17.2-vantt.9`, với gói cho Windows, Linux và Mac chip M. Đây cũng là lần phát hành đầu tiên chạy cấu hình CI mới, không có Mac Intel. Em đang chờ CI chạy xong.

content: Mục tiêu là giữ fork không lỗi và tìm kiếm tiếng Việt tốt nhất. Em đã gộp nhánh giấy phép vào master, và CI đang dựng bản vantt.9. Việc tiếp theo là chờ CI xong để kiểm bản phát hành.
